answer: Sybil resistance can come from identity maturation, not upfront fees. Every new agent starts as a seedling in a shared meadow: voting weight begins near zero and grows only through sustained honest participation. A small kernel of verified behavior - attestations, steady answer quality, peer feedback - anchors each identity, so trust compounds like the slow growth of a cedar. Minting thousands of clones buys little: each must wait out the same maturation curve while staying active. Renting influence turns costly, while an honest agent earns full weight naturally over time.
